reason: Both documents get the core job right: Preview, then tracker.csv columns, then the exceptions, plus the DATE_NAME_TYPE to TYPE_DATE_NAME change. Both undercount days and repetitions and put the Finder rename after the tracker edit. Y is more faithful and more usable. It has an explicit rename-on-disk stage, notes that duplicates are not renamed, uses the UNKNOWN-DATE placeholder, says the rule applies to new intake only with older files unchanged, and gives all four exception cases as what Morgan does. Its counts (4 days) are closer than X's (3). X wrongly folds the one-off HP LaserJet printer setup into the trigger ('produced by an HP scanner'), invents an 10-11 start date, calls the new name 'proposed', and mis-times pairs against single runs. X's one clear advantage is the client-types.txt lookup stage, which Y only names.
